description:
I'm a software developer interested in backend systems, AI, and open source. For Flame in Freefall, I want to explore how AI can turn NASA's combustion research into fire-safety insights.

Looking for teammates in ML, data science, computer vision, or data visualization. Curious and ready to build together? Join us!
summary: FlameLab is a spacecraft fire-safety research explorer for engineers and graduate students. It ranks NASA PSI combustion investigations (BASS, Saffire, FLEX, SAME, DAFT, and more) by relevance to a target atmosphere such as a Moon base, using deterministic, auditable scoring over seven factors never filling in missing evidence. Each investigation page pairs conditions, measurements, and prevention/detection/suppression implications with AI summaries where every sentence carries a citation to a real data field and every number is verified or dropped. Gaps, side-by-side comparison, and structured export support modeling, while hard guardrails -no partial-gravity predictions beyond the data, no crew procedures - keep outputs trustworthy. Fire behaves fundamentally differently in reduced gravity and exotic atmospheres, and Earth data does not transfer matters because it turns scattered microgravity experiments into grounded, citable answers habitat designers can actually build on.
details:
FlameLab is a spacecraft fire-safety research explorer. A user picks a target atmosphere (e.g. a Moon base at 30%+ oxygen, ≤10.2 psi) plus a lens — prevention, detection, or suppression and FlameLab ranks 11 curated NASA PSI combustion investigations (BASS, BASS-II, Saffire I–III, FLEX, FLEX-2, SAME, SAME-R, DAFT, DAFT-2) by relevance.

Ranking is a deterministic weighted sum over seven factors (oxygen/pressure overlap, airflow match, fuel relevance, hardware scale, gravity relevance, pillar fit), with weights and environment profiles in versioned YAML. Every result carries its per-factor breakdown, and missing evidence leaves a factor unevaluated - never guessed so removing evidence can never improve a rank. Each investigation page shows fuels, conditions, variables, and measurements alongside AI summaries where every sentence must cite a real record field ([rec:<id>#<field.path>]) an every number must appear in the cited field; a verifier drops anything unsupported. Gaps, side-by-side comparison, an oxygen–airflow conditions map, grounded Q&A, and structured export for modeling complete the three core journeys.

Benefits

• Turns scattered microgravity experiments into direct, citable answers for a specific habitat atmosphere.

• Explanations are auditable: scores show their breakdown, and assumption-vs-brief provenance is always visible.

• Fails closed: no invented numbers, no partial-gravity predictions beyond the data, no crew procedures -research context only.

Intended impact

Help engineers, equipment designers, and graduate students design prevention, detection, and suppression for Moon/Mars habitats and spacecraft from real combustion data instead of Earth intuition, and make the remaining data gaps explicit so future experiments target what matters.

Tools, languages, software

• Backend: Python, FastAPI, SQLite, Pydantic, PyYAML, httpx; pytest suite; Makefile workflow (run-api, validate-records, eval-si, check-gaps).

• Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, React Router (hash routing), D3 conditions map, custom SVG radar; Vitest + Testing Library, Playwright E2E, oxlint.

• Data: 11 hand-curated JSON records validated against docs/DATA_SCHEMA.md, sourced from NASA Glenn fact sheets and the researchers' combustion guide.

• AI layer: Meta Model API (Muse) with keyword retrieval, prompt templates in si/prompts/, citation verifier, audit log, and a 20+-case eval set (make eval-si).

• Hardware: none — runs on two localhost dev servers (API :8000, UI :5173).

Creativity

The creative core is "trust as a feature": a scoring engine that provably can't reward ignorance, an AI layer that deletes its own unverified sentences, and a UI that spotlights gaps and assumptions instead of hiding them. The conditions map, breakdown wheel, and comparison radar make relevance visible, not just numeric.

Factors the team considered

• Honesty over helpfulness theater: strict evidence policy, source: brief vs source: assumption labels, kill-switch (FLAMELAB_SCORING_ENABLED=off) that degrades gracefully.

• Safety scope: rocket/propellant fires and crew procedures are out of scope and redirected to mission safety authorities.

• Audience tone: clear, concise, technical, no hype.

• Reproducibility: golden rank tests, property tests (scores in 0–1, missing data never raises a score), versioned prompts/weights, and workflow checklists for curation, review, and release.
